Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures trained on audio spectrogram data are a powerful tool for the task of music structure analysis and in particular for the detection of boundaries between musical sections.

(1) Convolutional Neural Network models can be trained directly on mel-scale spectrograms to detect boundaries in audio signals; (2) the models can be trained with only a few annotated audio files and achieve state-of-the-art performance; (3) the models are robust against different annotation guidelines; (4) the models generalize to related tasks such that they can be trained to detect transitions between songs.
